No. The 67.7 ha loss is real, but it occurred in 2020, before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so it falls outside the post-cut-off period.

For 2021–2025, the tool detected no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more across the whole property (2,843.1 ha), with full valid satellite coverage. The only post-baseline loss was 0.4 ha in 2021, in patches under the 0.5 ha minimum, so it isn't counted as an event.

Other loss events (0.8 ha in 2008, 25.5 ha in 2015, 4.8 ha in 2017) are also all pre-baseline. The JRC map shows no forest in 2020.

Limits: this doesn't rule out all change, since very small or narrow changes at 30 m resolution can be missed. It is also not a compliance or EUDR finding, and it covers only the evaluated period.
